newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Police station site to star in HK gov't land sale.
newsitem.headline: Police station site to star in HK gov't land sale.

text.p: The public auction of a police station site in central Hong Kong this week is expected to be well received, riding on a recent surge in the territory's property market, analysts said on Monday.

The 1,223 square metre plot in the prime Causeway Bay district, slated for conversion into a commercial site, would be the focus of Wednesday's government land sale, they said. A smaller site across the harbour in Kowloon will also be offered.
"The police station plot is a significant commercial site, and on the back of recent sentiment, it should do fairly well," said a property analyst with an Asian research firm.
Analysts predicted the site would receive a thumping reception at between HK$691 million and HK$720 million.
"I won't rule out the bigger developers because we are talking about a built-up area of 200,000 square feet in recurring (rental) income," the analyst said.
While many analysts noted there would be a large amount of office space due for completion over the next two years, there was not as much on the drawing boards beyond that.
"There has not been a lot of land (made) available for office space for the last 12 months," said research manager Stephen Kidd with Vigers Hong Kong Ltd.
But the other plot, a 217 square metre site in San Po Kong for commercial and residential use, would less warmly received, analysts said.
They forecast it would fetch only HK$42 million to HK$59 million.
"It's just too small," Vincent Luk of James Capel said.
Hong Kong's property market has enjoyed a fierce surge in recent months and property shares have been central to the recent record-breaking run by the local stock market.

Although the government said on Monday it would monitor the surge in prices if they were found to affect the livelihood of the territory's residents, many analysts said they were bracing for a bull run for at least the whole of 1997.

"We are very positive on residential properties because of tight supply. We are looking for at least another good year ahead and another 20 to 25 percent rise in prices in the first quarter of next year," the analyst with the Asian firm said.
Large developers were likely to be even more enthusiastic over another government land auction on January 15, when three large residential sites would come under the hammer, James Capel's Luk said.
